corrections.notes:
For the 114° Semi-Peak Lapel shown in the image, the shape transitions between a traditional peak lapel and an exaggerated fashion peak. The very open 114° angle causes the peak to visually flatten and broaden, which is why many patternmakers call this a semi-peak rather than a true aggressive peak.

Image Characteristics

The image shows:

Peak angle marked 114°
Straight upper edge
Wide-open gorge geometry
Long spear-shaped lapel
Semi-peak appearance due to flattened peak angle
Similar visual style to 1930s drape-cut and some zoot-suit tailoring

Tailoring Interpretation

A 114° Semi-Peak Lapel is near the practical limit of classic tailoring geometry. The peak begins to flatten visually, creating a broad shoulder-emphasizing line rather than a sharply pointing peak. To maintain the look shown in your image, a 13 cm width, 5.5 cm projection, and 57° peak leg angle provide the closest geometric match.
